units.text: INT. PULLMAN DINING CAR - NIGHT
Snow hammers the windows.
The train has stood motionless for nine hours.
Brass lamps, white linen, a chandelier that sways in the wind.
ELIAS WHITCOMB, 60s, banker, silver mustache, sits stiffly at the head table.
A glass of brandy untouched before him.
HORTENSE BELLWEATHER, 50s, in black bombazine and pearls, knits a long grey scarf.
DR. SAUL RIVLIN, 40s, rumpled tweed, smokes a pipe by the window.
MISS CORDELIA PYE, 20s, a schoolteacher in a modest blue frock, sits with a book she isn't reading.
AUGUSTUS FLOYD, 50s, the porter, stands by the pantry door with a silver coffee pot.
Coffee, ladies and gentlemen?
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Nine hours, porter. When do we move?
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Conductor says dawn, sir.
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Conductor said midnight.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Conductors say a great many things.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Mrs. Bellweather, I think it's very cozy.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Cozy is a word for people who have never missed a funeral.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Is it your funeral, madam?
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: My sister's. Tomorrow at noon. In Chicago.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Silence.
The chandelier creaks.
Floyd, bring me a telegraph form.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: The wires are down, sir.
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: Then bring me a pencil and I shall write a letter to the president of this railroad.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: And how shall it be delivered, Mr. Whitcomb?
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: By a man with a sled and a sense of duty.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: There isn't one.
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: There never is.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Mr. Whitcomb, if you complain once more I shall put this scarf round your neck and pull.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: I beg your pardon!
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: You heard me.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Please. Please, both of you. It's only snow.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Whitcomb rises.
Chair SCRAPES.
Only snow! My daughter weds in Chicago tomorrow. I have not missed a day of work in thirty years. I have never been late for anything.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: And I have never been early for anything. Sit down.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: I shall not sit down!
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: He's shouting at the weather, Mrs. Bellweather. Let him.
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: I am shouting at you, Doctor! You, with your pipe and your sneer.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: I sneer only at men who deserve it.
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: Deserve it!
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Deserve it, indeed.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Deserve it? I built half the railroad this train runs on!
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Then you built it badly.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Sir, ma'am, please. The other passengers.
units.name: FLOYD

units.text: What other passengers? We are four, and a porter!
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Five, Mr. Whitcomb, if you count the dignity you've misplaced.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: I will not be insulted by a knitting widow.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: She's not a widow. She's a sister in mourning.
units.name: RIVLIN

units.text: I thank you, Doctor.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: Whitcomb slams his hand on the table.
The brandy topples.
Amber spreads across the white linen.
The room freezes.
Even the wind seems to hold its breath.
Mr. Whitcomb. You're shaking.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: He looks at his hand.
Then at the stain.
The anger drains.
My wife died on a train.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: No one speaks.
Floyd sets the coffee pot down, very gently.
Thirty years ago. In the snow.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: I did not know.
units.name: HORTENSE

units.text: No one does.
units.name: WHITCOMB

units.text: Hortense sets down her knitting.
She reaches across the table and lays the unfinished scarf in front of him.
Then it's yours. It will be cold in Chicago.
units.name: HORTENSE
